6th Annual Red Eagle Gravel Grinder

Sunday, May 16, 2027 – 10:00 AM Mass Start
Benefiting the Steven G. Cancer Foundation

Join us for the 6th Annual Red Eagle Gravel Grinder (REGG)—a scenic day of gravel riding through the beautiful back roads of Geneva, Ohio, all benefiting the Steven G. Cancer Foundation.

We’re excited to be back at Red Eagle Distillery for another year of great riding, great company, and great support for a great cause. Riders of all experience levels are welcome, with three route options:

  • 44-mile Classic Gravel Grinder
  • 22.5-mile Sprint Gravel Grinder
  • 12-mile Family Ride

About the Rides

  • Ride hard with friends or enjoy a relaxed cruise—your pace, your adventure.
  • All riders begin together at 10:00 AM in a mass-start, Gran Fondo-style rollout from Red Eagle Distillery.
  • Please note: This is a timed ride with posted results, but it is not a race.
  • New for 2026: Chip timing for all riders, with awards for the top three Female and Male finishers in both the 43-mile and 22.5-mile routes.
  • Expect a mix of gravel, chip seal, dirt, mud, and some pavement (about 55% gravel).
  • Gravel, cyclocross, mountain, single/fixed gear, fat tire, and tandem bikes are welcome. Road bikes are not recommended.
  • E-bikes are permitted but not eligible for awards.
  • All routes will be clearly marked; cue sheets and maps will be available.
  • Official routes will be posted on Ride With GPS:
    • Red Eagle Classic Gravel Grinder – 44 Miles
    • Red Eagle Sprint Gravel Grinder – 22.5 Miles
    • Red Eagle Gravel Family Ride – 12.5 Miles
  • Registered riders will receive Ride With GPS files the week before the event.
  • Roads are open to traffic—please ride safely and obey all traffic laws.
  • Helmets are required; front and rear lights encouraged.
  • Please respect the roads and your fellow riders—no littering.
  • Water & Fuel Stops:
    • 44-mile route: 2 stops
    • 22.5-mile route: 1 stop
  • A SAG vehicle will be on course for rider assistance.

What You Get

  • The pride of riding in one of Northeast Ohio’s premier gravel events—all while supporting AYA (adolescent & young adult) cancer patients through the Steven G. Cancer Foundation.
  • A Red Eagle Gravel beer glass for every registered rider—perfect for your post-ride beverage!
  • Post-ride celebration including:
    • One complimentary drink (yes…beer!)
    • A hot bowl of chili courtesy of Red Eagle Distillery & Black Door Tavern
    • Additional food available for purchase

EventName: 2027 International TASTE Series - BAROQUE SICILY, ITALY
EventNotes: Find all event details and updates on the event website: https://www.farmtoforkfitness.com

Route & Format

  • Start/Finish: Staging begins just west of Three Roads Brewery (312 W 3rd St, Farmville) on the High Bridge Trail.
  • Distance & Course: A 18.25-mile, out-and-back gravel time trial with the turnaround at the Prospect Road trailhead 9 miles out .
  • Surface & Terrain: The route follows the High Bridge Trail—an abandoned rail-bed with finely crushed limestone, minimal grade, and smooth packing
  • Historic Highlight: Although we don't race over the High Bridge many participants will warm up/cool down cross the iconic 2,400-ft, 125-ft-high High Bridge—Virginia’s longest recreational bridge and a Civil War landmark.  You can access this by riding east from the start finish.

    Race Operations

  • Individual Time Trial: Racers start individually. First racer will be 12 noon…all racers will start before 1230pm.. No drafting allowed
  • Amenities: Entry includes a race number, timing chip, and eligibility for overall and age-group awards, plus random giveaways.
  • Part of the Series: This event is part of the Virginia State Park Adventure Series

    What You’ll Experience

  • Scenic Beauty: Ride through rolling Piedmont farmland, tree-lined shaded corridors.
  • Trail Amenities: The trail is well-maintained, flat, and lined with facilities—parking and restrooms, and picnic tables exist at Prospect trailhead if you have some spectators to see you ½ way; water isn't available on the trail, so be self-sufficiency for the Time Trial.

    Strategy & Tips

  • Tire Choice: Smooth crushed limestone favors fast-rolling 40mm gravel tires—but 32–35mm cyclocross tires work too .  Participants have raced on TT, road, gravel and even mountain bikes.
  • Equipment/course: The course is mostly flat (rail-trail grade ~0.3%), but the turnaround means the course is two way from start to finish as usually protected from winds.
  • Hydration: Bring your own water—none is available on-trail.  They will be water available post event.

    Why It’s a Must-Ride

  • A perfect blend of speed and gravel adventure on a historic trail.
  • A well-supported event—with timed results, awards, giveaways.
  • Points for both the Virginia State Park Adventure series and the Virginia Gravel Series.

Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century

The event you've always known and loved... just got even better.

Welcome to the next chapter of one of Alabama's favorite gravel traditions. The Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century is everything you've come to expect—endless quiet dirt roads, Southern hospitality, and an unforgettable day on the bike—but with an exciting new home and an even bigger finish-line celebration.

For 2027, we're moving the start and finish to Historic Downtown Opelika, where race day will kick off with the energy of a community festival. Riders and spectators can enjoy local food trucks, craft beer from Red Clay Brewing Co., handcrafted cocktails from John Emerald Distillery, live music, vendors, and a vibrant downtown atmosphere before and after the ride.

Once you're out on course, it's still the Dirty Deluxe you know and love. We'll feature a 30, 60 and 100-ish mile route that showcases the best red clay roads, rolling countryside, and scenic backroads East Alabama has to offer. Along the way, expect the same welcoming volunteers, well-stocked aid stations, and the laid-back, grassroots feel that's made this event a favorite for over a decade.

We've also added a few fun new awards, expanded post-race festivities, and several surprises we'll be announcing as race weekend approaches.

To preserve the rider experience, registration will once again be limited to 350 participants. When it's full, it's full—so don't wait to claim your spot.

The Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century is proudly produced by James Bros. Bikes, with proceeds benefiting the Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation (AARRF).

About the Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation

The Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation (AARRF) is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by the owners of James Bros. Bikes after encountering countless abandoned dogs while riding Alabama's backroads.

AARRF exists to support the small, privately operated rescue organizations that work tirelessly to provide sanctuary, medical care, rehabilitation, adoption, and transportation for neglected and abandoned animals throughout Alabama. These rescues fill a critical gap in a state where animal welfare resources are often limited and many county shelter systems remain overwhelmed.

Every dollar generated through the Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century helps AARRF continue its mission of supporting these rescue partners and giving discarded animals a second chance.

When you register, you're not only signing up for an incredible day on some of the best gravel roads in the Southeast—you’re helping change lives, both on two wheels and four paws.

About the MTB 100

For 24 years, the Mohican MTB 100 has attracted riders from all over the world. The race begins in a mass start in downtown Loudonville, Ohio and finishes at Mohican Adventures one mile from downtown. Riders criss-cross three counties along a single loop, climb 10,000 feet, and go pedal-to-pedal with the top pros on this legendary ultra-endurance loop in Northeastern Ohio. The Mohican 100 features both a 100 mile and a 100-kilometer option with six fully stocked aid stations.

2026 Race Recap

More than 500 racers tackled this year's Mohican MTB 100, braving muddy trails and challenging conditions brought on by mid-day storms. Despite the obstacles, participants consistently express their enthusiasm for riding Mohican, where the finish line festivities provide a rewarding conclusion to the adventure. Know before you arrive

  • All Race starts, 100 mile, 100k and 50k begin in downtown Loudonville, Ohio beneath a large Mohican MTB 100 Banner and ends at Mohican Adventures (about 1 mile from downtown)
  • 100 mile or 100k loops consists of up to 10,000 feet of climbing along mostly singletrack, double track or dirt roads, spanning three counties through some of the most remote and scenic areas in the rolling hills of Mohican Country.
  • Climbs of nearly a mile, with elevation gains of 300+ feet, rock gardens, streams, and more.
  • The 100-mile course is planned to include five fully stocked and manned aid stations.

Yield to Horses

Public horse trail

Horses may be traveling along a short section of the Blue Trail from the end of the snowmobile trail, crossing SR97 to CR3234, about five miles past aid station one.

 

Notices have been posted requesting they avoid this section of trail until 1:00 p.m., but this is a public horse trail. If you encounter a horse, YOU MUST stop and walk your bike or pull your bike off the trail to allow them to pass.

 

Horses often view moving bicycles as predators and can panic, causing a danger to the rider. Be sure to talk to the rider as you approach and as they pass since this will help put the horses at ease. If an incident occurs because of your neglect of this rule you may be disqualified.

Drop bags

100-mile racers are permitted drops at your choice of aid stations 2, 3, 4. 100k racers can drop at 2. If you require special foods, it is recommended that you include them in your drop bags. Drop bags are located in your race packet and can be placed in the bins located at packet pickup on Friday AND Saturday morning. All drops will head to aid stations at 7am.

Level playing field

Since its inception in 2006, the National Ultra Endurance Race Series (NUE) has elevated the sport of ultra-endurance Mountain Biking to the national stage. It is dedicated to providing a level playing field for ALL riders, professionals and amateurs alike! No USAC or any other license is required. To become eligible for National Series rankings and rewards, racers need only complete THREE events to receive a national ranking and qualify for series awards. The Mohican MTB 100 has been a NUE series race from day one of NUE.

Welcome to the FINGER LAKES FRESHET! 

freshet /freSHet/ noun - the springtime rush of fresh water from melting snow.

BIG NEWS:  New DATE for 2027- Grand Depart is Memorial Day weekend, May 29, 2027! And we're offering two new short routes, and the long routes will be in the reverse direction from previous years!

More details on routes, parking, camping, GPS tracking, and other logistics will be sent to registered riders as the Freshet approaches. Also, all registered riders who sign-in will receive a Freshet 2027 handmade print in the mail.

This is a casual, unofficial, unsanctioned, and unsupported gravel bikepacking group or solo ride starting and ending in Stewart Park, Ithaca, NY, homeland of the Gayogohó:no people.  We have four routes available from 25ish miles up to 500ish miles!  The pace you set is your own, so take your time or ride fast, it's your call.  

The terrain between lakes and around the southern tier of the Finger Lakes tends to be very hilly, so expect plenty of climbing, on the order of about 100' per mile, or 1,000' per 10 miles. The routes are certainly challenging. Less than half the riders completed it in our first two years ('25 and '26 results are below). We avoid traffic as much as possible in our routing, but that means you can also expect some rough gravel, some singletrack, and some steep snowmobile trails.  This year, we have eliminated most of the hike-a-bike spots in favor of rideable sections, but we've kept some tough sections where they are essential to connect avoid main roads.  We'd rather hike-a-bike than share the road with cars, to be honest.  A burly gravel bike or a svelte mountain bike would be ideal.  We'd recommend knobby 38-60 mm tires.  

This ride follows the self-supported ethics of other bikepacking events like The Adirondack Trail Ride, Vermont Super 8, Catskill Bikepacking Route, or the Tour Divide – meaning it's an unmarked route, with no sag wagon, no planned feed stations, etc. And there probably won't be anyone at the finish line other than your friends and family.  If you wish to be “compete” for a fast time, the rules of self-supported races apply, where you can't receive aid from friends or family, but may utilize food, lodging, repair stations, as long as they are publicly available resources.  Otherwise, if you're touring it at your own slow pace, “cheat” as much as you like to ease the time.  

You can certainly ride fast if you like – but who's really in top shape in May? So we also encourage riders to view this as more of a social ride. To this end, we also provide at least one group campsite where participants can reconvene by a campfire and tell tales of the day's adventures. Riders who wish to push themselves physically and mentally may choose to do so, but will need to agree to be safe about it and be respectful of everyone they encounter en route – especially on rail trails where cyclists need to yield to all other users. If you want friends and family to be able to follow your progress in real-time, we'll have the routes on Trackleaders and facilitate SPOT rental (about $85) or the PING phone app (about $15). But riders aren't required to do this unless you want your official time posted or you hope to set an official FKT (Fastest Known Time) for a route. It's the only feasible way for us to fairly and accurately record times. As a bonus, the Trackleaders webpage holds an archived event replay for all tracked events, where you can follow along with the race and ride flow!  What a fun record!  

Route maps will be updated in January 2027. And regardless of which route you sign up for, you can switch routes if you're feeling more or less ambitious at any time during the ride.

Photos, including Rigs of the Freshet portraits, can be found on our Instagram page: https://www.instagram.com/fingerlakesfreshet/

EventName: The Original Growler Endurance Mountain Bike Races
EventNotes:
The Original Growler XIX

May 29-30, 2027

Gunnison, Colorado

Brought to you by Gunnison Trails and presented by Gunnison Valley Health, the Original Growler is the primary fundraiser for Gunnison Trails, a Colorado 501(c)3 non-profit organization. Gunnison Trails is dedicated to maintaining and expanding the singletrack experience in the Gunnison area since 2006. All proceeds from the Original Growler support Gunnison Trails and our trail maintenance and building efforts here in the Gunnison Valley. To learn more about Gunnison Trails, visit: gunnisontrails.org.

CLOCKWISE COURSE IN 2027

Since the first race back in 2008, the Original Growler has not wavered from our guiding principal of asking you to trade your hard earned dollars for three things:

1) An awesome day on the bike. The Growler offers a challenging, singletrack heavy mountain biking experience on some of the finest trails on the planet.

2) A killer party. Food, drink and camaraderie in downtown Gunnison (for those that still have some party left in them)!

3) Top shelf trails, both existing and developing. Regardless of where you live, you become a stakeholder in Gunnison area trails as every penny of your entry fee goes directly to the 501c3 non-profit, Gunnison Trails, and Gunnison Trails’ mission is focused solely on improving and expanding area trails.

The Original Growler showcases most of the trails at the Hartman Rocks recreation area on BLM public lands. “Hartmans,” as we call it, was chosen as one of the top 20 mountain biking destinations on BLM lands and offers a one-of-kind trail riding experience. If you have ridden Hartmans, you know all about the magic of these high desert trails.

If you haven’t, you owe it to yourself as an experienced mountain biker to test your skills and fitness on the trails at Hartman Rocks. You’ll be forced to alternate relentlessly between fast and flowy trails through seas of sagebrush to tricky and technical rock moves on islands of granite and in the many micro canyons that pock this primal landscape. While there are no big climbs and the total vertical gain isn’t remarkable, the seesaw nature of the Growler course is a supreme test of all around mountain biking. Go ahead, commit. But be prepared to challenge your mind, body and skills.

  • Saturday May 29, 2027 - The Classic (8am start), around 32 miles on dirt (limited to 350 riders), FREE Kids Race (8:30am start at the Hartman Rocks Base Area)
  • Sunday May 30, 2027 - The Pup (8am start), around 15 miles on dirt
  • Sunday May 30, 2027 - The Big Bad (8am start), around 40 miles on dirt (Sunday starters for the Pup and Big Bad limited to 350 riders) 

 

THE ORIGINAL GROWLER IS A DIFFICULT RACE. NO BEGINNERS, PLEASE!

The Original Growler is a tough, singletrack heavy affair and is for experienced mountain bikers only. This includes our shorter Pup 20 route. Riders must possess the skills and judgment necessary to assess technical, difficult and challenging trails and roads and get up, down, over and through them safely. This says nothing about the fitness that is required simply to ride this course. Additionally, the Growler is a backcountry race so you could be far from medical help if you get injured. Please come to Gunnison prepared!

Registration opens at 8pm MDT Sunday, December 1st, 2026.  

Refunds and Transfers: The Original Growler’s only reason for existence - along with offering you an epic challenge and an amazing experience - is to raise money for Gunnison area trails, trail advocacy and other local non-profits.

2026 Refund Policy: Full refunds are available until March 31, 2027 at midnight. Refunds will only be granted if we receive an email at info@gunnisontrails.org prior to this date and time. In this email you can also request a partial refund, contributing an amount of your choice to the Gunnison Trails cause. Thanks in advance for that!

From April 1, 2026 to May 15, 2027 at midnight, a full refund, less a $25 contribution to Gunnison Trails, is available. Again, you must email us at info@gunnisontrails.org within this time period and you can also contribute more than $25 if you choose, just let us know in your email.

Apologies, but there will be no refunds after May 15, 2027. However, check out our transfer policy below as we will allow transfers until May 23, 2027.

Transfers: Transfers will be allowed until May 23, 2027 at 5pm. We have set up our registration platform at bikereg.com to allow users to edit their registration. This will allow you to log on and change categories, team name, rider's name and contact details, etc. This will also allow you to transfer your entry to another rider if you're unable to race and have someone who can take your place.

Confirm your receipt: TRIPLE check to make sure your race is in your CART and your payment shows the correct FEE. We've had a few racers who ‘thought’ they placed their race in their cart but didn't (ending up with say: a donation, maybe a jersey and no race registration). Avoid this mistake and double check your cart before hitting the checkout button.  
Also, a waitlist confirmation is just that (a $0 receipt)…it doesn't confirm you actually purchased a race registration. If a waitlist spot opens, we will move you into your category, and you will be charged then.  

FREE KIDS RACE! FUN FOR THE WHOLE FAMILY…

Calling all young mountain bikers from Striders on up that want to participate in the Gunnison Trails' Growler weekend but just don't quite have the legs for a big race lap. We are thrilled to partner with CB Devo to offer this challenge for younger riders, ensuring fun for the whole family! You can sign your kiddo up at our packet pickup on Friday evening, or at the Hartman Rocks Base Area Saturday morning. Full details can be found at originalgrowler.com/kids-race/

Full Original Growler details, including a super helpful FAQ section, can be found at our website HERE.

IMPORTANT EVENT DAY INFORMATION

There are many important details to ensure the safety of our riders and volunteers. Please read everything in it's entirety.

Note: Information is subject to change. Please check back often.

 

We will have bicycle mechanics set up at the start line and then will mobilize after the start of the rides and set up at some of the rest stops. Please make sure you are getting your tune-ups done now prior to the ride!

 

This event is rain or shine!! We do not offer refunds.

 

FINISH LINE PARTY

The Finish Line Party starts at 11AM and ends at 4PM

Food is provided by the infamous Jean-Louis Lepage

Beverages provided by: TBD

Post-Ride Ammentity: Living Water Showers will be set up and offering FREE showers to riders post event. The showers are first come first serve. There are 6 stalls and time is limited to 15 minutes per person. Please feel free to bring a change of clothes and utilize the showers for a fresh rinse off post ride. They'll provide everything else like toiletries, towels, etc. 

Band: TBD

Recovery Specialist: TBD

Many vendors to check out as well will be set up!

Questions? Want to be a vendor? Email us: biketourdefrederick@gmail.com

 

KNOW BEFORE YOU GO!!

Please note: No biking shoes will be allowed inside of the fire hall on ride day. Please plan accordingly with a change of shoes.

 

Parking & Traffic Flow – Please be sure to carefully follow the traffic patterns as they may have changed from previous years. There is plenty of free additional parking in the grass once the asphalt lot fills up. Please be aware of your surroundings when entering and leaving the fire hall to make sure there are no cyclists around you.

 

COURSE NOTES:

 

The Century route will be marked with WHITE arrows, the Metric Century with GREEN arrows, the Club Ride with ORANGE, and the Family Ride with PINK arrows.

Please take a cue sheet with you before you leave. These will also be available at the Fire Hall.

 

Ride with GPS: You can create a free Ride with GPS account by visiting https://ridewithgps.com/. All routes are uploaded and viewable/downloadable on the app. 

 

WHAT TO BRING:

  •  Please bring an ID (required for alcoholic beverages) and money for additional drink tickets, merch, etc. (please avoid using cash)

  • Lawn chairs and/or a blanket to use while enjoying the finish line party.
  • A change of clothes. We will have Living Water Showers set up at the Finish Line Party and you are welcome to use their shower stalls to rinse off post- ride. All towels and toiletries included!! 
  • A water bottle. All rest stops will have 5 gallon jugs to refill with water and/or Gatorade. 
  • Your phone (fully charged is helpful!)
  • Your helmet. Helmets MUST be worn at all times. 
  • Repair kit that includes an extra tube that fits your bike.

RIDING SAFELY:

 

1) Please be sure your bike is in good, working order before you arrive. If in doubt, take your bike to a shop to get a tune-up. We recommend The Bike Doctor, The Bicycle Escape, or Blue Ridge Bicycles. Their mechanics will be available on Saturday at the event for last minute checks such as pumping up tires, patching holes, etc and they will be stationed at some of the rest stops. 

 

2) You MUST wear a helmet. Riders without helmets will NOT be allowed to ride or will be removed from the course if seen riding without a helmet.

 

3) Do not ride more than two abreast. Many of these roads are narrow country roads. Please do not take up a whole lane of traffic by riding more than two abreast. SAG vehicles have been told to break this up if they see it on course. When riding through Gettysburg National Military Park on the Century route please ride SINGLE FILE. 

 

4) Obey ALL traffic laws. If you see a red light or STOP sign...you must stop! The roads are not closed, and you will be riding with vehicles on the road. Riders seen breaking traffic laws will be removed from the course.

 

REST STOPS:

 

There will be a total of 6 rest stops on the course. Century riders will pass all 6, the Metric will pass 4, and the Club Ride will pass 2. When you are entering or leaving a rest stop, make sure you know your surroundings and signal or tell people what you are doing to avoid an accident. Make sure to thank our great rest stop sponsors/volunteers who are out there to support you!

 

Water, PowderVitamin, peanut butter & jelly sandwiches, granola bars, and bananas will be at every stop and each stop will have their own special treats for riders. Rest stop times will also be printed on the cue sheets.  

 

There is a small “rest stop” along the 10 mile family route in Heritage Farm Park. There will be some snacks and sodas for the participants.

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

 


The Breakaway Benefit Cycling Festival is the cornerstone fundraiser for the Connecticut Cycling Advancement Program (CCAP) and directly helps us provide hundreds of kids with access to cycling and cycling teams all across the state. The CCAP started in 2013 and has grown to be a national leader in the development of youth cycling programs with teams in schools and regions across the state. In the last twelve years, we've served thousands of kids and orchestrated hundreds of events in over 50 towns. Annually, over 350 youth riders participate across 40 programs in mountain biking, road cycling, and cyclocross. Additionally, the CCAP hosts over 25 youth race events and skills clinics annually. With your support, you're helping create more school and municipality-based youth cycling programs and helping the CCAP get thousands more kids on bikes, so please join us on this fun-filled day, pedaling bikes and enjoying time with family!

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

Fundraising Awards

All Breakaway Benefit attendees are eligible for AMAZING fundraising awards, which are compounding, meaning the more you raise, the more you get! Our top prize is oh-so-worth it and people will be jealous of your incredible style for years to come.  To be clear, this is not a fundraising minimum. 

Take a look at last year's Fundraising Tips Packet (2027 coming soon) to see all of the sweet CCAP prizes you can earn by going that extra mile in fundraising for Connecticut's youth cycling. Hint: it's all in our famous limited-edition ice cream design.

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

This is the Breakaway Benefit:

  • Gravel and Mountain Bike Rides for ALL: Enjoy Connecticut's most beautiful and scenic roads during fully supported rides of different lengths. Our Gravel Sampler is perfect for a beginner to novice rider and is fully marked, so there is no need for a navigation device if you don't have one. The Big Scoop offers fun for riders of all abilities but is a bit longer - ride at your own pace or have fun cruising around with friends - just remember, roads are open to traffic.  Mountain bikers, will be riding the beautiful trails at Norbrook Farm Brewery with ride lengths of multiple distances; expect routes as short as 5 miles and as long as 12. We will have two coach-led routes so need to memorize the trails.
  • A Theme to Remember: Check out this last year's famed and unique Breakaway Benefit Ice Cream Kit, which will serve as inspiration for all of our other swag items available at different levels (more info below in the fundraising packet)
  • Festival: This isn't just a ride! We'll have a team tent zone, kids' games, product vendors, and more bike-focused fun to keep you entertained throughout the day. CCAP staff, along with a DJ/live music, will be on hand to lead the fun!
  • Delicious Food and Drink: Riders are welcome to enjoy a light, pre-ride arrangement of pastries and coffee, then we will kick off the ride with a quick ceremony of Fundraising Awards (including top fundraiser and top junior fundraiser)! Enjoy the ride and then join us for lunch, a live DJ, and games to celebrate their riding, fundraising, and accomplishments.
  • Want to volunteer? Please visit our Volunteer Page to sign up! All volunteers will receive complimentary breakfast, and lunch after the ride! No fundraising is required for volunteers, however, it is encouraged. For volunteer questions, please reach out to volunteer@ctcyclingadvancement.com.

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

The Breakaway Benefit Ride is dedicated to the memory of David Hoyle; and honors him with our ever-changing ice cream design. As the Executive Director of CCAP, Dave was tirelessly working to provide kids and their families with the opportunity to ride bikes. He was an advocate for the sport, a healthy lifestyle, and embodied the highest level of humility and kindness to all whom he came across. He will forever be in our hearts.

Please join us in celebrating Dave and the wonderful impact he had on the Connecticut cycling community with a fun, family-filled day on bikes!

Those who want to fundraise in memory of Dave and ride are encouraged to do so by signing up for any ride distance and rising above and beyond the fundraising requirement! Those who DO NOT wish to ride but want to attend are encouraged to volunteer or sign up for the non-cyclist fundraising category.

#ridelikedave

Timed Segment Details

Individual Timing Details: The Breakaway Benefit Gravel rides are as competitive as you want them to be, rip it, ride it, or just have fun. Participation is not required to ride. Keep in mind, this is not a race; it's a fundraising ride. Roads, while lightly trafficked, are open to traffic, so riders MUST abide by all local traffic laws (don't run stop signs, cross the center-line of the road, etc). Details for fondo style timed segments:

  • 5 Timed Segments (1-2 Miles in length)
  • Results are the lowest cumulative time through all segments - riders must complete all 5 segments to be eligible for awards
  • Segment Start/Finish will be marked with signage
  • Top 3 Men / Women awards for Big Scoop Gravel
  • Winner recognition for Individual Junior Boys/Girls (U19); 45+ Men/Women; 55+ Men/Women for Big Scoop Gravel
  • Breakaway Gravel Sampler segment results are for fun
  • Preview timed segments here
  • Team Competition - Bring your Teammates (more details below)!


Team Competition Details: There will be a team competition. To be eligible, each member must register with their team affiliation. Team membership will be determined based on the ‘Team/Club/Company’ field during BikeReg checkout. Please ensure all team members use the same name for your team.

Rules are as follows: 
  • Men and Women categories.
  • Men must have a minimum of four riders; women must have a minimum of three riders.
  • There is no maximum number of riders one team can have. Bring everyone.
  • Only riders who enter and complete the Big Scoop course and all five timed segments by 2 p.m. will be scored
  • The time of the fourth fastest rider of each men’s team in each segment will be used for scoring. The aggregate of those scores will be tabulated for the team’s result.
  • Only the time of the third fastest rider of each women’s team in each segment will be used for scoring. The aggregate of those scores will be tabulated for the team’s result.
  • Any combination of riders on a team can be scored. For example, a team may have different riders scoring in each segment.
  • The overall individual results have no bearing on the team competition.
  • Only one men’s and one women’s team will be awarded the team competition.

EventNotes:
3 Feet Cycling will once again be offering SAG Support services in Emporia, KS June 6, 2027 supporting the 200-mile and 100-mile events. Our services include local knowledge of the course prior to race day, answering any questions you may have, drop bag services, minor mechanical services, power washer, water, soft drinks, nutrition, cooling towels and encouragement to get you to the finish line.  All you need to focus on is riding your bike to the finish line and 3 Feet Cycling will take care your race day needs.  

If your day doesn’t go as planned, it’s ok! One of the many 3 Feet Cycling team members will pick you up and drive you to the finish line in Emporia. Plan on bringing your phone with you and the 3 Feet Cycling SAG number will be provided during bag drop. If you have someone local that is waiting for you, we encourage you to always share your location on your phone or when the phone signal is available. 

Our team members have been providing support for riders since 2016 in the Flint Hills and many have completed the 100-mile and 200-mile events along with other gravel endurance races. Our services speak for itself, and we’ve been fortunate enough to support many podium finishers in several age groups and overall winners. We continue to refine and improve our process of what we offer, and we love to support all our riders and listening to their race day stories. 

**there are no refunds of fees if you choose to defer or not participate. We do offer to defer your support to the following year if you would like. You need to email us by May 29th, 2026 to be issued a credit for the following years support. 

Watch our team in action at Checkpoint 1 in Eureka, KS in 2022. https://youtu.be/BMMbN485tzs

 

Rules require you to have someone available to pick you up if you abandon. Event organizers will NOT come pick you up. 3 Feet Cycling is not an official partner of Lifetime or Unbound Gravel.

The Great Descent is the mountain bike race LA needed. A true mountain adventure For all the mountain bike junkies, are you down to descend 10,000ft of elevation while finding your way along jagged cliffs , thru creeks and along jungle brush.

This route will cover some of our epic mountain bike routes running 50 miles with 10,000ft of descending and 5,000ft of climbing. 

This is a point to point route that starts out at the highest peak we could find that still has great single track and ends all the way back at Let's Ride Cyclery.

finish address is 1819 W Burbank Blvd, Burbank, CA, 91506
 

We have routed an epic one way route that is 90% dirt and only 10% paved.

 Start location is 34.34363° N, 117.98321° W, Race starts at 8am, check in will start at 7am

It is on you to get to the starting line, we do not have a shuttle van yet. Make plans to be dropped off or to have a ride to pick up your car from the start.

The Rules

 

  • This is a set route you will need to follow and there will be a time cutoff, we cant wait forever for you to finish.

  • You must ride the full route exactly, and under your own power,  no catching a ride.  At the finish we will be checking all finishers gps info to verify completion of the route.

  • There is no parking at Let's Ride Cyclery, please use the side streets behind the shop or make plans to be dropped off and picked up.  

  • The bike you start off on is the bike you finish on, no changing bikes allowed.

  • There is no sag vehicle to pick you up and take you home.   Have a plan and tell someone. 

  •  NO E-Bikes

  •  All registrations are FINAL, No Refunds.

  • You can transfer to another rider during the transfer window only, this Must be done before event date, Thank you for your understanding.

EventNotes:
About The Race + Ride

Presented by Steuben Brewing Company, the Keuka Lake Gravel Classic will host hundreds of riders from all over the country as they traverse the challenging and scenic dirt roads of the Finger Lakes beer and wine country.

The KLGC offers three course distances that will feature vistas and vineyards, soul-crushing climbs and gnarly descents. The routes offer fast hard racing for traditional elite and masters racers and exciting challenges for granfondo riders and new cyclists alike.

Following the races, all riders are invited to celebrate at our after party featuring prizes, music, food, and the region's finest craft beverages at Steuben Brewing Company.

About The Courses

Join our Strava Club for course maps and race updates!

The Comet, The Cascade and The Nugget courses begin at Steuben Brewing Company and wind through old vineyards, beautiful gravel roads and scenic mixed surface roads; All along the route catching glimpses of Keuka Lake.

After a short warm up, riders climb the first of several challenging hills through one of the country's oldest wine regions. This epic climb, where there is sure to be a crowd of cheering locals, leads to the first ridge crest of the day before dropping into some seasonal roads.

At this point in the ride, the course splits with The Cascade course riders getting some pavement relief before tackling some more rolling gravel roads.

The Comet course riders are just beginning the challenges as they connect to the old Prattsburgh Gravel Classic course and race the beautiful Urbana State Forest. The Comet riders will then reconnect with The Cascade course for a series of rolling paved and dirt roads before making their way back to Steuben Brewing Company for the finish and after party. 

The Nugget course-This course will feature a lighter ride for those interested in gravel but aren't quite sure of their comfort level or maybe are recovering from an injury. The roads will be mixed surface roads and gravel with some rollers and flats to enjoy with one long descent. Leading out of the brewery we will head toward a section from the old Prattsburgh Rambler. The focus for this ride is to help grow the gravel community and bring people together. All proceeds from registration and fundraising for The Nugget course will benefit a regional charity. This year's charitable donation will be going to Empowering People's Independence! EPI's mission is to “empower people with disabilities, neurological, and chronic health conditions to pursue the life of their choosing.” They offer comprehensive services across 22 counties in Upstate New York, including the Finger Lakes, Western NY, Southern Tier, and Central NY regions.

About Steuben Brewing Company

The Finger Lakes best brewery, Steuben Brewing Company, offers incredible craft beers brewed with 100 % New York State ingredients in the heart of the region’s best riding and hiking terrain.

Owner, Chad Zimar a life-long residents of Keuka Lake and advocate for the local cycling scene. Chad loves to share his passion for the outdoors as the brewery offers a cycling club and regular hiking adventures. Join them for a group ride and learn more about the brewery. Pedal For Pilsners Cycling Club

Race Rules

Violations of any of the rules below could lead to being DQed! Promoter reserves the right to shift start times, change course layout, and combine fields based on safety issues and field sizes. Be sure to check your pre-race email for all final details before race day.

All riders must wear a helmet

All courses are open to traffic so follow the rules of the road.

Do not litter on course.

Be cool to everyone: Course marshals, volunteers, other racers, spectators, locals etc. A lot of people work hard to put this together, help us continue it by being cool.

You can race any bike you want (as long as it’s not an e-bike) but we recommend a gravel, mtb or cross bike. Road bikes are not advised.

No e-bikes in the competitive field. 

Much of the gravel is rocky and loose with some big stones on descents. We recommend a wide tire of 38mm - 40 mm.

Some people ride and some people race and that’s cool, but if you’re not going to race please line up towards the back of the field at the start line.

Keep Fat Bikes Fat: bikes in the Fat Bike Division should have 3.8-inch tires or wider. Racers who enter a plus-sized mtb bikes will be DQed.

The Nugget course is non-competitive and is a fundraiser for Empowering People's Independence!  Donations can be made here and during registration checkout. All riders must follow the rules of the road at all times. Ebikes are legal in this field.

EventNotes:
Back for 2027!

The Nation's eyes turn towards Virginia once again this summer as Roanoke will be hosting National Mountain Bike Championships in July! As in 2025 and 2026, they are hosting all endurance events - Cross Country, Short Track, and Marathon. With this, we are excited to offer Race Camp in order to provide ambitious junior racers from around the country the opportunity to preview the courses while receiving insight and preparation tips from top professionals and course designers. 

Each day of camp will focus on the specific courses that will be raced in July. Each venue will be visited and the campers will work with coaches to break down individual sections, analyzing line choices and developing race strategies. There will also be dedicated blocks for hot laps and mock races to allow campers to experience the courses with a true competitive mindset. 

In 2027, all campers will have the opportunity to tap into performance analysis from Slay. Slay is the first integrated, data-driven athlete education system in cycling with the mission of building complete athletes through a multi-pillar educational pathway. One of the most exciting aspects is all camp participants will receive in-depth analysis of their performance on each course, section by section, and be able to develop concrete strategies for improving performance on race day.

2027 Race Camp is being held at Hollins University, which is conveniently located near the XCO and XCC courses, and serves as the start and finish of the XCM races. Campers will have the privilege of utilizing the University's grounds, dormitories, and dining hall. Each evening will also include seminars from regional professionals with topics ranging from race nutrition to detailed event preparation. 

Our new camp location will allow greater flexibility of camper schedules throughout the week. Those focusing on XCO will continue to have daily access to those courses, and now XCM competitors will be able to spend multiple days  previewing and breaking down the extended course.

The Eagles Mere Grand Cru Gravel event is a non-competitive gravel weekend all about community growth. Ride as many or as few of the looping courses as you like. All of the loops will all be well-marked and supported taking you through covered bridges, scenic vistas and forgotten roads. We’ll have food, fun and music in Eagles Mere Village and you’ll have time to visit the shops and museums in town.

All are welcome!

All abilities and experience levels are invited. Our Grand Cru Crew can recommend routes for any adventure. Maps and GPS routes will be provided. Courses will be marked as well as aid stations and rovers will be out.

This event is produced by Eagle's Mere Village and the Lycoming County Composite high school mountain bike team. Proceeds from the event will go to support the Sullivan County community and the Lycoming County Composite mountain bike team.

EventNotes:
Indiana's BIKE PARTY is back for 2027!!!  Pedal Putnam ‘27 returns with all the vibes you’ve come to enjoy plus the chance to earn points towards Indiana's Race Series, take home some of the $1,000 CASH PRIZE, claim your PR, or make some great memories with great friends … plus, donuts!  

Pedal Putnam is more than just a bike race.  It's a VIBE.  It's COMMUNITY.  It's the great atmosphere you get to experience with friends, family and other riders on or around bikes.  Whether it's the TEAM awards, the pre-race donuts from Breadworks or the post-race festivities at Lost Hollow Beer Company … we are here for the party.  Are you?

Pedal Putnam is a growing GRAN FONDO event aimed at the beginner, the racer and the weekend enthusiast.  Whether you're looking to complete your first Gran Fondo, race against the best, or get in some great training miles before RAIN or Dust Bowl, this event is for you.  Featuring three different routes (100k, 43 miles & 12.5 miles), there's a course for everyone.  Even better, all three will take you past some of Putnam County's murals, including the new ones.   We're excited to see Putnam County become central Indiana's backyard and a destination spot for arts, culture and food.  And while many people have gotten to experience Putnam County's gravel scene, Pedal Putnam will give you a taste of our open roads.  

 

Race/Ride Routes

The Mural Metric (62 miles)

For the 100K (62 miles) event, riders will be competing for overall placings and (NEW THIS YEAR) age-group placings:  open men's, open women's, Master's Men & Women (30's, 40's, 50's, 60's, 70+).  Trophies and prizes will be awarded for each category.  Results will be timed thanks to Racemaker productions.  The Mural Metric will once again head west before circling back through Clinton Falls, up to Bainbridge and around Heritage Lake before returning home.  The course will feature a lead vehicle to protect the pointy end, well marked turns and caution points, as well as great SAG support like last year.

 

The 43 Mile Route

Our 43 mile route will still feature plenty of climbing (~2,000 feet), and give you plenty of chances to soak in the best of Putnam County:  covered bridges, sustained climbs, and rolling hills.  Prizes will be awarded for top three men's & women's riders + Master's men and women (45+).  Again, all riders will be timed.

 

The 12.5 Mile Route

Finally, our 12.5 “Scenic” mile route will allow you to see the highlights of the Putnam County Mural Project, including the famous grain silo murals, take you out to Big Walnut Sports Park and bring you back to Greencastle on some county roads.  No prizes for this option.  Just the enjoyment of a great day on a bike and maybe your first bike event!  The scenic route also allows you to ride through DePauw University, Indiana's premier liberal arts college.  NEW THIS YEAR … riders will be able to enjoy the NEW Campus Connect trail from DePauw University out to Ivy Tech, taking away the first few miles on Veteran's Highway.

 

Pedal Putnam FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ's):

 

1. Is Pedal Putnam a race or a ride?

 

Great question. It's both! Pedal Putnam is a chip-timed Gran Fondo cycling event similar to the Boone County Classic, Ride Across INdiana (RAIN Ride) or the Hancock Flat 50.

 

Since it is timed, some will compete, especially since there are prizes for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in the overall category (men's & women's) as well as age-groups (30's, 40's, 50's, 60's & 70+ // men and women). Last year, Amir Danel and Sarah Watkins won the men's and women's 62.3 mile race respectively (see results here).

 

But, I can't emphasize this enough ... you don't have to race. Riders will separate out according to ability very early in the ride, and with three different routes, you can choose how far and how hard you want the ride to be. The goal of Pedal Putnam is simply to get as many individuals and teams out on bikes as possible, all in support of Putnam Parks & Pathways

 

2. Is Pedal Putnam a road ride or gravel ride?

 

Pedal Putnam is a road ride/race.  THERE ARE NO GRAVEL ROADS (but there may be chip-and-seal).  All of the roads on the three routes are paved roads, although some of the county roads do have some gravel in corners or are chip-and-seal surfaces.  Last year, we had riders on road bikes, TT bikes, recumbent bikes, tandem bikes, single-speed bikes, mountain bikes, gravel bikes.

 

3. Will the ride have support/SAG stops?

 

Yes, all three routes will have SAG stops. The 62 mile "mural metric" will have three SAG stops, the 43 mile will have 2, and the 12.5 mile will have one SAG stop. All SAG stops will feature hydration from Tailwind nutrition + water + energy bars/granola bars/bananas and more.

 

4. What do I get with my registration?

 

By registering at www.bikereg.com/pedal-putnam by June 1st, you'll get a FREE Pedal Putnam t-shirt, plus a registration bag full of other great offers and local info on some great Greencastle eateries. Registration is $70 until Dec. 1 & $80 until Feb. 1st for the 62 and 43 mile rides. Then it jumps to $90 on Feb. 1st. The 12.5-mile ride is a constant $30 and still includes the t-shirt ??

 

5. What if it is raining?

 

Pedal Putnam is an all-weather event within reason obviously. Barring severe weather forecasts, the ride will roll out at 8 am for the 62, 8:15 am for the  43 mile and 8:30 am for the 12.5 mile riders.

 

6. Will the course be marked?

 

Yes! Thanks to Putnam County Visitors Bureau, we have great signage for Pedal Putnam, including the bright green for the 62 mile, blue for the 43 and red for the 12.5 mile rides. HOWEVER, riders should strive to have a GPS device or phone WITH THE ROUTE loaded or saved to their device. While we will mark the course, it has happened where signs have been blown over or removed.

 

7. What about bike safety and vehicles on the road?

 

Pedal Putnam is an open-road ride/race, which means ... Rule #1 ... BE SMART and BE ALERT. In other words, don't be "that person"! The aim of this event is to support cyclists AND to foster more riding in Putnam County. That means showing drivers our best behavior. That also means you will be expected to follow all normal traffic laws. At certain, high-traffic intersections, local police and the Putnam County Sheriffs Office Indiana will be stationed to monitor and assist cyclists and motorists to ensure safety. On the 62 and 43 mile route, the major intersection will be at 231 at Brick Chapel. Most of the course, though, will occur on county roads. Cyclists are expected to stay in the appropriate lane and allow for cars to pass as needed. The 62 mural metric includes a lap around Heritage Lake Association - a beautiful loop featuring new pavement. The 62 and 43 mile ride/race will have a police escort for the first few miles out on West Walnut road before turning north where a lead vehicle will stay in front of the 62 mile leaders ONLY. The 12.5 mile will include a police escort through DePauw University and out to the People Pathways before coming back to town on county roads.

 

You will be responsible for yourself out on the ride, although we encourage riders to look out and check on each other. A race support number will be provided closer to the race that you can call in the event of a major mechanical. As with most other bike events, riders will reach out to 911 in the event of a major medical emergency or injury.

 

8. What is happening before and after the ride?

 

Pedal Putnam will begin with a packet-pick-up at Lost Hollow Beer Co. on Friday, June 11th from 4 to 7 pm, and you're encouraged to check out Greencastle's wide range of great restaurants or eateries while in town.

Then, on the race/ride day, we're blessed to have Breadworks By Bridges providing pre-race donuts. Following the race, Lost Hollow Beer Co. will be provided post-race brews and we will have various food truck vendors along with a Kona Ice Truck for your post-ride hunger.

 

Your participation goes a little bit further in 2026.

Our event has partnered with Friends of the Park of Putnam County, Inc. (FOTP), a local 501(c)3 organization dedicated to the development and sustainability of outdoor recreation in Putnam County. Over the past few years, Friends has been involved in several projects, including the Putnam County Mural Project, Hamrick Station trail expansion, and the lighting of Robe-Ann Park for the Winter Wonderland Lights Festival.


FOTP is on a mission to create a $500,000 endowment for the county to leverage. To that end, it
will receive a portion of the revenue generated from this event. In the coming years, this funding will be
used to purchase land for trail and park development, generate additional outdoor events, and generally
support the growing County Parks Board.


If you are interested in learning more about FOTP, please, visit their website at:
https://putnamparks.org/friends/
